speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks very swollen. To help me understand what's wrong, tell me: do you seem to pass gas or have bowel movements, and does the pain make you cry or pull your legs up?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description. Since the pain worsens with touch and he is fussy, has he been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow? Also, please tell me if his stools have changed in color or consistency, specifically if you notice any white, clay-colored stools. REQUEST TEST: Stool_for_bilirubin_and_occult_blood.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the results. Since his stool color is normal and not clay-colored, let's check for a surgical emergency: does he have episodes of intense crying where he pulls his legs up, and have you noticed "currant jelly" stools or blood in his diaper? Please also tell me if there has been any recent fever.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The combination of an 8-month-old male, intermittent colicky pain with leg-pulling, vomiting, and an X-ray showing dilated bowel loops with an empty rectum is highly specific for intestinal intussusception. Please proceed with an urgent Ultrasound to confirm the diagnosis and guide reduction.
